nodes.label: The Development Kit
nodes.rationale: An index is only useful if there is something to point to: setup, conventions, testing, architecture overview, workflows and release guide are the minimum every repo gets.

nodes.label: README.md Index System
nodes.rationale: Every docs folder needs a README index with a status column so agents can skip irrelevant files without opening them.

nodes.label: Revert-on-main Rollback (toolkit-clone)
nodes.rationale: History is never rewritten on main; the revert lands through a PR like any other change.

nodes.label: toolkit-clone Release Target
nodes.rationale: Every merge to main ships this target; a clone's binary reads assets live from the clone, so clone users get edits on the next git pull.

nodes.label: install.sh Never Rebuilds an Existing Binary
nodes.norm_label: install.sh never rebuilds an existing binary
nodes.rationale: install.sh builds bin/devexp only when it is missing, so Go changes need `rm bin/devexp` first; asset edits need no rebuild because a dev build reads assets live from its checkout.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md as Indexer
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md loads into context every conversation, so every inlined line costs token budget and goes stale while the docs/ equivalent stays current.

nodes.label: Kit Before Index (Order Matters)
nodes.rationale: /devxp builds the kit before CLAUDE.md; generating the index first leaves it nothing to link to, which is exactly how knowledge ends up inlined.

nodes.label: Evidence or [CONFIRM]
nodes.rationale: Every command cites where it came from; anything detected but unproven is written [CONFIRM] rather than a plausible guess.

nodes.label: Degradation When No Guide Exists
nodes.rationale: Grooming marks targets unverified, /deliver reports readiness unverified, and /release offers /devxp and otherwise cuts only — degrade, never refuse.

nodes.label: /release Never Improvises
nodes.rationale: It runs only what the guide says and refuses a [CONFIRM] step; a wrong guide is fixed with /devxp, not worked around at release time.

nodes.rationale: Fields are defined by the MCP struct in cli/internal/mcp/types.go; the installer ignores any other key.

nodes.label: --reinstall-mcps Config Refresh
nodes.rationale: Already-registered MCPs are skipped by default, so a changed entry needs a forced remove-and-re-add.

nodes.label: required_env Gating
nodes.rationale: A missing key skips only that MCP with a [REQUIRED] warning rather than failing the whole install.

nodes.label: http / sse Transport
nodes.rationale: streamable-HTTP is the current protocol and preferred; sse is only for legacy SSE-only servers. The installer registers the URL but never starts the server.

nodes.label: Self-Contained MCP Process (mcp-ui-inspector)
nodes.rationale: The MCP launches and manages its own backend on demand instead of installer-managed venvs or Docker; it ships as its own repo because 'a distribution repo should distribute, not host a build'. Installer-managed Docker services were removed with the Python install scripts.

nodes.label: devexp.config.json (repo root)
nodes.rationale: A missing file is a warning, not an error.

nodes.label: DEVEXP_DIR
nodes.rationale: The only way to point a release binary at a checkout; it must carry the .devexp-toolkit marker plus agents/, skills/, mcps/ or install stops rather than falling back.

nodes.label: KIMI_CODE_HOME
nodes.rationale: The Kimi root is written into installed agent and skill bodies, which are prompts, so a value with control characters, ${...} forms or invalid UTF-8 would inject or corrupt text in every agent and is refused.

nodes.label: Kimi Code CLI Target
nodes.rationale: Hook scripts are copied into $KIMI/hooks/ rather than run from the checkout, because Kimi reads a command it cannot run as an allow — a moved or deleted clone would silently disarm every guard.

nodes.label: Kimi Feature Subset
nodes.rationale: An agent body replaces Kimi's whole system prompt (hence the ${base_prompt} marker), unknown tool names are dropped silently, allowed-tools is ignored entirely, hooks fail open, one invalid [[hooks]] entry disables them all, and a project .mcp.json can shadow a devexp server.

nodes.label: Kimi mcp.json Fingerprint Merge
nodes.rationale: Kimi has no command to edit mcp.json and rejects the whole file if one entry is invalid, so devexp validates every entry against Kimi's schema before replacing the file and rewrites only entries whose recorded fingerprint still matches. ${VAR} is resolved at install time because Kimi expands nothing when reading this file.

nodes.label: devexp.config.json Customisation
nodes.rationale: Committed to the fork so it travels with the repo and applies on every ./install.sh, avoiding a per-engineer setup step.

nodes.label: Fork and Upstream Merge Workflow
nodes.rationale: Conflicts are rare because the config is a separate file from the agents and skills.

nodes.label: Org-Internal MCP Entries
nodes.rationale: Same schema as mcps/registry.json entries; a missing required_env key skips only that MCP and the rest of the install continues.

nodes.label: MCP Secret Precedence
nodes.rationale: mcps/.env wins over the shell environment, which wins over an empty placeholder in registry.json.

nodes.label: Asset Root Resolution
nodes.rationale: Order is $DEVEXP_DIR, then (dev builds only) the verified checkout the binary was compiled from, then the embedded assets extracted to the user cache. The cwd and the binary's location are never searched, so a release binary can never be silently pointed at an untrusted tree.

nodes.label: Model Precedence
nodes.rationale: --model flag > devexp.config.json "model" > the CLI's own default.

nodes.label: Ticket Platform Adapter
nodes.rationale: Fetch/update/save/retrieve operations are abstracted behind one adapter table (Linear, Jira, GitHub Issues, Notion, none) so the rest of the workflow is written once and stays platform-agnostic.

nodes.label: Postmortem Action Items
nodes.rationale: Every item must be specific, measurable, owned and dated across detection/prevention/mitigation/process, otherwise follow-through cannot be tracked.

nodes.label: Contributing Factors
nodes.rationale: Conditions that let the root cause have impact are tracked separately from the root cause itself, and speculation belongs here rather than in the root cause section.

nodes.label: Epic Decomposition
nodes.rationale: 3-8 atomic tickets of 1-3 days each, dependency-linked with an identified critical path, so the sequence of work is decided before any ticket is created.

nodes.label: Conventional Label Vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Only existing labels are used unless clearly necessary, keeping the taxonomy stable across tickets and platforms.

nodes.label: Issue Tracker Platform Detection (project-manager)
nodes.rationale: Detection result is cached in agent memory so the priority table (Linear MCP, Jira MCP, gh, glab, none) does not have to be re-run on every call.

nodes.label: 5 Whys Analysis
nodes.rationale: Stops only at a human decision, missing process, design flaw or environmental constraint, because the root cause is almost never a single line of code — it is the condition that made that line fail.

nodes.label: Service Topology Discovery
nodes.rationale: Service names, start/stop commands, health checks, log locations and the deployment mechanism are read out of docker-compose, k8s manifests, Makefile, Procfile and CI workflows so the runbook's steps are verifiable.

nodes.label: Do Not Fabricate History
nodes.rationale: If git log does not explain why something was done, the guide says 'origin unknown' rather than guessing — a confident wrong origin is worse than an admitted gap.

nodes.label: Where We Got Lucky
nodes.rationale: Always included because near-misses are where the most valuable prevention work is usually found.

nodes.label: Mandatory Rollback Section
nodes.rationale: Operations without a documented rollback path create incidents, so every runbook must reverse itself.

nodes.label: Placeholder Policy (never fabricate a command)
nodes.rationale: A runbook containing a fabricated command is worse than no runbook because it creates false confidence during an incident; every command must be sourced from the project's real configuration and anything unfound is written as an explicit [FILL IN] placeholder.

nodes.label: devexp-plugin.js opencode Entry Point
nodes.rationale: The entry composes only modules listed in the installed selection file so authors never edit it; registration happens through the registry instead.

nodes.label: devexp/hooks.json Selection Contract
nodes.rationale: An empty array can only be an installer bug (with every hook disabled no plugin is installed at all), so `[]` is treated like an unreadable file and blocks every tool call.

nodes.label: Legacy opencode Flat Install Cleanup
nodes.rationale: Cleaned up only after the new plugin installed successfully, so a refused install leaves the old one working; a file is removed only if its name is one of the 9 legacy names AND its content carries that file's devexp header.

nodes.label: opencode Feature Subset
nodes.rationale: Agent/Skill/Task* tools, persistent agent memory and terminal colours are dropped at transform, so agent-spawning skills such as /deliver and /improve run degraded.

nodes.label: Hand Tools an Absolute Edited Path
nodes.norm_label: hand tools an absolute edited path
nodes.rationale: An absolute path is never read as an option; tool-specific quirks remain (jest reads a bare path as a regex, ruff expands @argfile after --, vitest drops file filters after --).

nodes.label: Never Spawn Synchronously in opencode
nodes.rationale: opencode runs plugins inside its server process, so execFileSync/spawnSync freezes every session until the tool exits.

nodes.label: C2 — /improve Repo-Wide Hygiene Sweep
nodes.rationale: The only path that prunes agent memory, because memory pruning needs codebase-navigator's drift classification.

nodes.label: /release — Cut and Ship
nodes.rationale: Stands alone as well as being /deliver's hand-off, so a deferred or externally-gated release can be resumed; before it existed the only options were re-running /deliver or releasing by hand, which is how stray worktrees pile up.

nodes.label: Cut vs Ship
nodes.rationale: Cut happens once per release behind one confirmation and stays local until the tag push; ship happens once per affected target with a gate per target and per production-facing promote stage.

nodes.label: Release Target
nodes.rationale: A separately shipped artifact. Encoding per-kind ship/rollback differences in the skills would make them vendor-specific and wrong for most repos, so each repo declares how it ships in one file and the skills read it.

nodes.label: Target States
nodes.rationale: shipped/skipped are retirable; awaiting-external, blocked and failed keep the delivery's artifacts, so a ticket stays live to /cleanup and /improve even when its branch is merged and its ticket closed. State persists at ~/.claude/agent-memory/release/<ticket>.md.

nodes.label: Cleanup Safety
nodes.rationale: The single shared reference all cleanup paths point at; each skill carries concrete guards inline because each runs standalone, and this doc is the rationale they must not diverge from.

nodes.label: Skill Naming and Merge-Over-Split
nodes.rationale: Short kebab-case names with no namespace prefix; closely related concerns merge into one skill with sub-sections (improve covers five concerns) rather than proliferating fine-grained skills. The same pressure keeps specialist capabilities as agents.

nodes.label: Skill vs Agent Distinction
nodes.rationale: If the work needs to read files, run tests and make changes independently it should be an agent; skills only shape the current context.

nodes.label: Confirm or Log Every Destructive Action
nodes.norm_label: confirm or log every destructive action
nodes.rationale: Silent deletion is forbidden; in an already-confirmed mode a line-by-line log stands in for the prompt.

nodes.label: Dry-Run First
nodes.rationale: A sweep that deletes before reporting is never correct; cleanup is reversible only by not having run it.

nodes.label: Memory Needs a Staleness Reason
nodes.rationale: Agent-memory entries are pruned only with a drift justification from the A1 Drift Classification; re-verified entries are re-dated, only resolved/contradicted ones removed.

nodes.label: Preserve on Failure or Doubt
nodes.rationale: A worktree with uncommitted work, a plan for an open ticket or a release state with an unshipped target is kept and reported rather than removed.

nodes.label: Never Touch Shared or Unscoped State
nodes.norm_label: never touch shared or unscoped state
nodes.rationale: Project-shared agent memory, the main checkout and the default branch are off-limits; globs must not match shared files even on an empty match set.

nodes.label: Target Detection by File Shape
nodes.rationale: Detection is by kind of file, never by brand, so the model stays vendor-neutral.

nodes.label: Go Toolchain Pinning (go1.26.8)
nodes.rationale: cli/go.mod's toolchain line is the minimum for local builds; with GOTOOLCHAIN=auto an older Go downloads it, with =local you need Go >= 1.25.11. CI and release install exactly go1.26.8 via go-version-file.

nodes.label: govulncheck Exit Code Policy
nodes.rationale: 0 = findings present but nothing called; 3 = a called vulnerability, the job fails; anything else is infrastructure (network/proxy), not a finding, and is re-run rather than fixed.

nodes.label: Vulnerability Scan (scripts/govulncheck.sh)
nodes.rationale: Scanned once per release platform because reachability differs per platform — a linux/amd64-only scan could miss a call that ships in the darwin binary.

nodes.label: cli Release Target
nodes.rationale: Built by goreleaser on a v* tag push and published to GitHub Releases; binary users get asset edits only in the next tagged release because goreleaser stages and embeds assets at build time.

nodes.label: Cut Procedure (tag is the version)
nodes.rationale: There is no version file — goreleaser injects the tag's version with -X at build time and local builds report `dev`.

nodes.label: Weekly Scheduled Scan and Its Failure Modes
nodes.norm_label: weekly scheduled scan and its failure modes
nodes.rationale: An advisory published while main is quiet would otherwise wait for the next push. The cron is 27 6 * * 1 because GitHub drops scheduled runs at high-load times. The email IS the alert, and its recipient silently moves to whoever last edited the cron or re-enabled the workflow; GitHub disables schedules in a public repo after 60 days of inactivity, which is the one way this can go quiet.

nodes.label: CI Gate on the Tagged Commit
nodes.norm_label: ci gate on the tagged commit
nodes.rationale: main has no branch protection, so the tag can be pushed while ci still runs on the release commit; since #155 release.yml calls ci.yml and goreleaser needs: that call, so the gate is on publishing rather than on tagging. The suites run again because the tag can precede CI, and the scan again because an advisory can appear in between.

nodes.label: Draft-Then-Publish Release Object
nodes.rationale: /release creates the GitHub Release as a draft right after the tag push so nothing is public and Latest does not move; with release.use_existing_draft goreleaser finds it by name, keeps its CHANGELOG notes, uploads assets while still a draft and only then publishes.

nodes.label: Hotfix-Forward Rollback (cli)
nodes.rationale: A pushed tag and its release are never deleted or moved because users may already have installed them and remote-install.sh pins by tag; marking the bad release pre-release makes releases/latest fall back.

nodes.label: hooks/registry.json Entry
nodes.rationale: The registry is the single source of truth tying a hook's Claude Code script and opencode module together, so a module without an `opencode` mapping is never installed and the entry point never needs hand-editing.

nodes.label: Wizard vs Non-Interactive Install Mode
nodes.rationale: chooseInstallMode(flagsProvided, isTerminal): the wizard needs no flags AND a TTY; --model alone does not count, and with no TTY a bare run installs everything for every detected CLI instead of prompting.

nodes.label: Known Coverage Gaps
nodes.rationale: No coverage threshold; runWizard needs a TTY (0%), config.Load and the claude mcp exec paths are untested, and the three graphify-* hooks have no tests at all.

nodes.label: Hand-Rolled PTY Test Helper
nodes.rationale: A real pty is the only way to test stdinIsTerminal's true direction (every other test stubs it); it is hand-rolled on golang.org/x/sys/unix rather than pulling in a pty module.

nodes.label: Map-Keyed Table Test Shape
nodes.rationale: No test calls t.Parallel() because t.Setenv/t.Chdir panic in parallel tests.

nodes.label: Absolute HOME Requirement
nodes.rationale: Every install destination is built from HOME, so an unset, empty or relative HOME would resolve targets under the current directory; install and uninstall refuse and touch nothing.

nodes.label: No Mock Library — Isolate With Real Resources
nodes.norm_label: no mock library — isolate with real resources
nodes.rationale: Files go in t.TempDir(), env/PATH/cwd through t.Setenv/t.Chdir, CLIs through executable stubs; logic behind a TTY prompt is extracted into a pure function so it can be tested without a terminal.

nodes.label: A Hook Is Three Touch Points
nodes.norm_label: a hook is three touch points

nodes.label: devexp Hook
nodes.rationale: Hooks intercept tool calls for safety guards, quality enforcement and audit trails; they are deliberately NOT for AI reasoning or external APIs — that belongs to agents or skills.

nodes.label: dangerous-cmd-guard Execution-Time Enforcement
nodes.rationale: The hook blocks an unanchored wildcard delete in a sensitive dir even if a skill's inline guard is wrong, so a prefix-anchored glob is the only form that will actually run.

nodes.label: Advisory Hook (Fail Open but Loud)
nodes.rationale: PostToolUse / file.edited handlers run after the tool completes and cannot block, so they exit 0 on internal error but must still print the error.

nodes.label: Byte-Exact Path Extraction
nodes.rationale: $(...) trims trailing newlines, which are legal in file names, so Python writes a one-character suffix that bash strips.

nodes.label: Queued file.edited Dispatch
nodes.rationale: opencode has no file.edited plugin hook, so the entry adapts `event`; handlers are queued rather than awaited so the event publisher is never held while a linter or test runner works.

nodes.label: Guards Always Hard-Block
nodes.rationale: Soft blocks add friction without a safety guarantee because the user can just approve them; 'ask' is legitimate only for reversible operations such as large-file-guard. opencode has no 'ask' at all.

nodes.label: python3 -I Interpreter Isolation
nodes.rationale: Hooks run with the project as cwd; isolated mode stops the interpreter importing anything from the project and ignores PYTHON* vars and user site-packages. Hooks use only the stdlib, so nothing is lost.

nodes.label: Silent on Success
nodes.rationale: 'All clear' messages would print on every tool call, so a hook that finds nothing wrong produces zero output.

nodes.label: Treat Tool Input as Data, Never as Code
nodes.norm_label: treat tool input as data, never as code
nodes.rationale: Every value in tool_input is untrusted; expanding it into program text (python3 -c, eval, unquoted expansion) is injection. Pass it on stdin, as argv, or through the environment.

nodes.label: Validate the Identifier First
nodes.rationale: The id must be non-empty and match [A-Za-z0-9_-], aborting the step otherwise, because a path-traversal or glob character would escape the intended directory.

nodes.label: Prefix-Anchored Glob Requirement
nodes.rationale: A leading * right after the directory boundary collapses to a blanket wipe the instant $id is empty (/tmp/*"$id"* -> /tmp/*), and reads identically to a deliberate /tmp/* to any safety check.

nodes.label: Hook Command Quoting (Claude Code)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code runs a hook command through sh -c, so before #135 a path with spaces or shell syntax was split or expanded — the hook did not run and, since Claude Code treats that as non-blocking, a guard failed open. Such paths are now registered as one POSIX single-quoted word.

nodes.label: Four CI Test Suites
nodes.rationale: ci.yml runs test (Go), hooks (three script suites) and govulncheck on PRs, pushes to main, a weekly schedule and every v* tag — release.yml calls it through workflow_call, so the same jobs are the release gate.

nodes.label: Installer Script Test Suite
nodes.rationale: uninstall.test.sh never runs against the real HOME — it uses env -i, a temp HOME and stub binaries, because the script deletes real files; remote-install.test.sh uses a stub curl so a refusal can be proved offline.

nodes.label: Mirrored Hook Test Pair
nodes.rationale: Every Claude Code hook test has an opencode twin covering the same cases, so the two implementations cannot drift apart.

nodes.label: Fail-Closed Guard Contract
nodes.rationale: An empty extracted value would make every check pass, so a guard that cannot read its input must exit 2 and print `internal error`; swallowing the interpreter error turns a crash into 'nothing to block'.

nodes.label: Proof of Work (DEVEXP_SCAN_PROOF)
nodes.rationale: A stand-in python3 or grep on PATH could report success without scanning, so the guard passes a token to the scanning program and only trusts output that carries it back.

nodes.label: Scan Budget
nodes.rationale: Claude Code does not block a tool call when a command hook times out, so a slow guard fails open; the budget plus a registry `claude_code.timeout` above it keeps the guard inside its window.

nodes.label: Reproduce the Caller, Not Just the Callee
nodes.norm_label: reproduce the caller, not just the callee
nodes.rationale: The first kimi runner.test.sh mirrored runHook alone, fed the pre-conversion camelCase payload, and passed 7/7 against a shape Kimi never sends while the real adapter refused every real tool call.

nodes.label: Link Over Duplicate
nodes.rationale: Duplicating documented content causes drift: the docs change but CLAUDE.md does not.

nodes.label: Custom Agents Are Read, Never subagent_type
nodes.norm_label: custom agents are read, never subagent_type

nodes.norm_label: three install targets (claude code, opencode, kimi code)

nodes.label: Kimi Honours Less — Installer Announces the Gaps
nodes.norm_label: kimi honours less — installer announces the gaps

nodes.label: SKILL.md Frontmatter (name, description)
nodes.rationale: `name` must match the containing directory exactly and becomes the slash command; `description` is what Claude reads when choosing a skill, so vague wording breaks routing.

nodes.label: Numbered Phase Pattern
nodes.rationale: The most reliable structure for repeatable behaviour across invocations; each step must be executable, not advice ('understand the codebase' is not a step).

nodes.label: Skill (Behavioral Overlay)
nodes.rationale: A skill is context injection into the current conversation, stateless and with no independent tool access — it shapes behaviour rather than running autonomously.

nodes.label: Triggered by Section
nodes.rationale: Creates a readable dependency map; without it nobody can tell whether the skill is safe to rename or change.

nodes.label: Verification Checklist Pattern
nodes.rationale: Checklists create accountability so Claude works through items rather than guessing when it is done.

nodes.label: When to Use Section
nodes.rationale: Acts as a routing contract for orchestrators and a discovery aid for users.

nodes.label: Orchestrators Absorb Specialist Commands
nodes.rationale: Users should not need to learn sub-commands: the six lifecycle skills invoke specialist agents automatically, and the old fine-grained slash commands map onto orchestrator phases.

nodes.label: Every-Caller Audit (Phase 6b)
nodes.rationale: Callers not listed in the plan are a regression waiting to happen, so every caller of any function whose signature changes must be grepped and enumerated.

nodes.label: Dynamic and String-Based Reference Scan
nodes.rationale: Import scanners cannot see reflection, registries, config-driven wiring, event names or documentation references, and those invisible couplings are what cause real regressions.

nodes.label: Dependency Risk Scoring
nodes.rationale: Score by consequence, not count — one caller in the auth path outweighs twenty in test utilities.

nodes.label: Migration Audit Report
nodes.rationale: Each breaking change is classified AUTOMATIC / MANUAL / risky with file and line, so effort and human-judgment needs are visible before any edit.

nodes.label: Stop Transitive Tracing at API Boundaries
nodes.norm_label: stop transitive tracing at api boundaries
nodes.rationale: HTTP handlers, queue consumers and CLI entry points are natural blast-radius limits; tracing past them yields unbounded graphs with no added decision value.

nodes.label: Incremental Execution with Verification Gates
nodes.rationale: A migration that breaks production is worse than no migration, so changes are applied in a strict order (dependencies, config, codemod, entry points, application code, tests) with a verification gate between each group and no code touched before the plan is confirmed.

nodes.label: Indexer Hard Limits
nodes.rationale: <=150 lines, no code blocks, no section over ~15 lines, every docs/ pointer resolves — checked by gen-indexer and update-indexer, and waived only inside devexp:preserve blocks.

nodes.label: devexp:inherit Block
nodes.rationale: Looked up in every ancestor CLAUDE.md up to $HOME, nearest id wins, optional `remote` ERE matched against origin. An existing preserve block with the same id always wins, so a changed parent block reaches existing repos only if the preserve block is deleted first.

nodes.label: devexp:preserve Block
nodes.rationale: Some directives are owned outside the repo (a family rulebook, an org policy); without a marker a refresh would read them as leaked knowledge and move or drop them.

nodes.label: Disabling Now Removes
nodes.rationale: A disabled agent/skill is excluded from the install set entirely, so it is treated as stale and deleted on the next run instead of merely not being updated.

nodes.label: .devexp-manifest.json Ownership Manifest
nodes.rationale: Tracks which agent/skill files (plus opencode plugin files and Kimi mcp.json entries and hook scripts) devexp installed, so later runs can remove what the toolkit no longer ships. Upgrading from a pre-manifest version records a baseline, so cleanup starts on the second run.

nodes.label: Stale-File Cleanup
nodes.rationale: Only a bare name devexp installed, still present byte-for-byte under the exact recorded spelling and still the kind devexp installs, is removed — so a corrupted or hand-edited manifest, a case-folded duplicate on APFS, or someone else's file can never be deleted.

nodes.label: Atomic Save (WriteFileAtomic)
nodes.rationale: Temp file in the same directory, fsynced, given the target's mode and renamed over it, so an interrupted save leaves the old or the new file, never a partial one. Symlinked config files are followed and the final target replaced so the link survives; dangling links, loops, non-regular targets and EXDEV renames are refused.

nodes.label: settings.json Ownership Rules
nodes.rationale: devexp owns only the {type: command, command: <script path>} handlers it registers; a handler with `args` or another type is the user's, and a settings.json that cannot be edited without losing something makes install stop with an error where earlier releases replaced the whole file.

nodes.label: Symlink Policy (Install Through, Never Remove Through)
nodes.norm_label: symlink policy (install through, never remove through)
nodes.rationale: A symlinked agents/, skills/, commands/ or plugins/ usually points at dotfiles or a source checkout, so devexp writes through it but lists stale entries to remove by hand and keeps them in the manifest until the link becomes a real directory. Removals go through an os.Root handle so a directory swapped mid-run cannot redirect them.

nodes.label: Git Archaeology
nodes.rationale: Historical context is the highest-value section of an onboarding guide because it is the one thing that cannot be read from the code and otherwise lives only in people's heads.

nodes.label: Known Gotchas and Known Debt Sections
nodes.norm_label: known gotchas and known debt sections
nodes.rationale: A gotcha without a recorded origin will be 'fixed' by the next person who meets it, and an explicit known-debt list stops engineers from churning on things that are intentionally deferred.

nodes.label: Performance Anti-Pattern Catalog
nodes.rationale: Catalogued by layer (database, application, frontend, infrastructure) so scanning is systematic; findings must carry an estimated gain because 'this might be slow' is not actionable and premature optimization is explicitly excluded.

nodes.label: Comment Triage (Implement/Ask/Flag/Skip)
nodes.rationale: A reviewer's comment is a request, not an order; sorting comments into implement, ask, flag and skip keeps architectural suggestions out of the current PR and forces ambiguity to be resolved by a human instead of guessed.

nodes.label: Review Severity Dimensions
nodes.rationale: Critical / Important / Minor / positive notes are evaluated in severity order, and 'Approve with minor comments' is valid only when every finding is outside the PR's own diff — minor describes severity, not scope.

nodes.label: Competing Falsifiable Hypotheses
nodes.rationale: At least three falsifiable hypotheses are generated and tested in likelihood order so the first obvious cause is not mistaken for the origin.

nodes.label: Canonical Examples Extraction
nodes.rationale: Memory stores only the file paths of canonical examples, never their content, because the files must be re-read each time to catch drift.

nodes.label: OWASP Top 10 Category Scan
nodes.rationale: Only findings with a concrete code path are reported — theoretical issues without evidence are excluded — and framework docs are pulled first so 'correct' is calibrated to the stack before anything is called a vulnerability.

nodes.label: Cross-Agent Deduplication
nodes.rationale: Several agents often describe one underlying problem from different angles; merging them is the highest-value step, and a finding flagged by two or more agents is upgraded one severity level because it is more confirmed.

nodes.label: Finding Priority Score Formula
nodes.rationale: Final Score = (Severity x 3) + Source Count + Confirmed-by-Evidence, giving one deterministic ranking across heterogeneous reports.

nodes.label: Severity Normalization (P0-P3)
nodes.rationale: Each specialist agent uses its own severity vocabulary, so all findings are mapped onto one P0-P3 scale before they can be compared or ranked.

nodes.label: Debt Categories
nodes.rationale: Code, architecture, test, documentation, dependency and infrastructure debt are discovered by separate phases so no class of debt is silently omitted from the register.

nodes.label: Debt Priority Score
nodes.rationale: Priority Score = (Carrying Cost x 2) + Business Risk + (1 / Fix Cost), so cheap fixes with high ongoing cost rise above expensive cosmetic work.

nodes.label: Architecture Decision Record
nodes.rationale: Status / Context / Decision / Consequences / Alternatives Considered, auto-numbered under docs/adr/ with the index README updated and superseded rows relinked; every ADR must list at least two alternatives because 'we considered nothing else' is never true.

nodes.label: API Contract Design
nodes.rationale: Every endpoint documents its error responses and every field its type and constraints; an API must never require the consumer to know internal IDs or implementation details.

nodes.label: Design Review
nodes.rationale: Judged on correctness, scalability, fit with the existing architecture, operability, simplicity and failure modes, with BLOCKING/MAJOR/MINOR concerns — feedback must be quantified, not 'this won't scale'.

nodes.label: Engineering Standard
nodes.rationale: Standards are derived from surveying 5-10 existing examples rather than invented, so they do not impose patterns the codebase does not already use successfully; each standard names its enforcement mechanism.

nodes.label: Database Schema Design
nodes.rationale: Indexes must justify themselves with the query they serve, ON DELETE behaviour is always explicit rather than left to database defaults, and migrations over 1M rows must state the lock contention risk.

nodes.label: Trade-off Analysis
nodes.rationale: Criteria are defined and weighted before options are scored, and the recommendation must name the decisive factor and what is being accepted as a tradeoff rather than restating the comparison table.

nodes.label: Atlas Freshness Gate (Drift Classification)
nodes.rationale: A cached codebase atlas is only trusted after classifying drift (CURRENT / SMALL / BIG) against its Last updated date, so a stale atlas cannot silently poison grooming while a current one adds no latency; the classification rule is referenced from codebase-navigator rather than duplicated.

nodes.label: Validate Before You Plan
nodes.rationale: Tickets are written by humans and AI without full codebase context and are frequently wrong, so every claim (file, function, version) must be verified against the actual codebase before it can appear in a plan; planning on unverified claims turns ticket errors into bugs and wasted work.

nodes.label: Plan Validation Anchor (commit SHA stamp)
nodes.rationale: Every path and line number in the plan was verified against one specific commit; recording the full SHA and branch in the plan body means the anchor travels to every persisted copy and lets the deliver phase detect drift and decide whether the plan is still trustworthy or needs a re-groom.

nodes.label: Mocks Are a Red Flag
nodes.rationale: Tests that mock the target will silently pass after a breaking signature change, so they give false safety and must be flagged explicitly rather than counted as coverage.

nodes.label: Blameless Postmortem Principle
nodes.rationale: Humans make mistakes and that is expected; attributing failure to systems, processes and conditions ('the deploy script lacked a rollback check') rather than individuals keeps the document a learning artifact instead of a punishment document.

nodes.label: Read Full File Before Applying a Suggestion
nodes.norm_label: read full file before applying a suggestion
nodes.rationale: A reviewer may have been looking at a partial diff, so a suggestion is implemented only after reading the surrounding file; if the suggested code is demonstrably wrong the intent is implemented correctly and the deviation is noted.

nodes.label: A Diff Is Never Enough
nodes.rationale: Reviewing only changed lines cannot tell code that is right from code added by someone who did not understand the system, so the full file, its callers, its tests and the codebase's existing patterns are read before judging the change.

nodes.label: Merge-Base Diff Against Remote Refs
nodes.rationale: Fetching first and diffing origin/<base>...origin/<branch> with three dots ensures the review sees only commits unique to the branch, not divergence in the base that happened since branching, and not stale local refs.

nodes.label: Read Before You Write
nodes.rationale: The quality of scaffolded code is entirely determined by how well the existing patterns are understood, so nothing is generated before the atlas and at least two canonical examples are read; generic boilerplate output counts as failure.

nodes.label: Conflict Resolution Framework
nodes.rationale: Contradictions are decided, not listed: safety beats performance, architecture beats convenience, explicit constraints beat preference, and specific file:line evidence beats speculation — hedging would leave the team with the same 'N reports, no answer' problem.

nodes.label: Frame Debt in Business Terms
nodes.rationale: Carrying cost, fix cost and ROI are the language that gets refactoring prioritized; 'this function is too long' is not a debt item, and style preferences are excluded because they have no carrying cost.
